Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/testguide.html | Test-running options > Testing for open files
Original text: any open file(s) that throw ``ResourceWarning`` (except the specific ones already ignored) would fail the affected test(s).
Atomic rule: Close every file a test opens so no unhandled ResourceWarning is raised.
Section context: "The ``filterwarnings`` settings under ``[tool.pytest.ini_options]`` in the ``pyproject.toml`` file has an option which converts all unhandled warnings to errors during a test run." - the consequence is a test failure, configured in pyproject.toml.
Notes: Enforcement: pytest filterwarnings error config in pyproject.toml.

Original text:
``pytest`` has the following test discovery rules:

 * ``test_*.py`` or ``*_test.py`` files
Atomic rule: Name test modules ``test_*.py`` or ``*_test.py``.
Section context: "Consult the test discovery rules for detailed information on how to name files and tests so that they are automatically discovered by pytest." A file outside the pattern is silently never run.
Notes: Conformance obligation stated once for files; the function and class patterns are separate rows because they govern different objects.

Original text:
``pytest`` has the following test discovery rules:

 * ``test_`` prefixed functions and methods
Atomic rule: Prefix test functions and methods with ``test_``.
Section context: Same discovery-rules list; a non-prefixed function is collected by nothing and silently never runs.
Notes: none

Original text:
``pytest`` has the following test discovery rules:

 * ``Test`` prefixed classes (without an ``__init__`` method)
Atomic rule: Give test classes a ``Test`` prefix and no ``__init__`` method.
Section context: Same discovery-rules list. The parenthesis is load-bearing: a Test-prefixed class with an __init__ is skipped by pytest.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/testguide.html | Where to put tests > Package-specific tests
Original text: Each package should include a suite of unit tests, covering as many of the public methods/functions as possible.
Atomic rule: Cover as many public methods and functions of the sub-package as possible with unit tests.
Section context: "as possible" is the only bound offered; no coverage threshold is stated anywhere in the docs or in pyproject.toml.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/testguide.html | Where to put tests > Package-specific tests
Original text:
These tests should be included inside each sub-package, e.g::

    astropy/io/fits/tests/
Atomic rule: Put a sub-package's tests in that sub-package's own ``tests/`` directory.
Section context: The example gives the exact path form ``astropy/io/fits/tests/``.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/testguide.html | Where to put tests > Package-specific tests
Original text: ``tests`` directories should contain an ``__init__.py`` file so that the tests can be imported and so that they can use relative imports.
Atomic rule: Include an ``__init__.py`` file in every ``tests`` directory.
Section context: The reason is stated as a consequence: without it the tests cannot be imported and relative imports break.
Notes: Fires only when a PR creates a new tests directory.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/testguide.html | Where to put tests > Interoperability tests
Original text:
Tests involving two or more sub-packages should be included in::

    astropy/tests/
Atomic rule: Put tests that span two or more sub-packages in ``astropy/tests/``.
Section context: none
Notes: Applies only if the new test exercises more than one sub-package.

Original text: Any time a bug is fixed, and wherever possible, one or more regression tests should be added to ensure that the bug is not introduced in future.
Atomic rule: Add a regression test whenever you fix a bug.
Section context: "wherever possible" sanctions omission. CONTRIBUTING.md's checklist states the same obligation unhedged under Testing.
Notes: Applies only if the PR fixes a bug. Same obligation as CONTRIBUTING.md 'Tests' bullet - conflicting strengths.

Original text: Regression tests should include the ticket URL where the bug was reported.
Atomic rule: Include the URL of the reported issue in the regression test.
Section context: none
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a regression test.

Original text: Tests that need to make use of a data file should use the `~astropy.utils.data.get_pkg_data_fileobj` or `~astropy.utils.data.get_pkg_data_filename` functions.
Atomic rule: Access data files in tests through ``get_pkg_data_fileobj`` or ``get_pkg_data_filename``.
Section context: "These functions search locally first, and then on the astropy data server or an arbitrary URL" - the named functions are the only sanctioned access path.
Notes: Restates the codeguide 'Data and Configuration' rule for the test context.

Original text: Tests that may retrieve remote data should be marked with the ``@pytest.mark.remote_data`` decorator
Atomic rule: Mark any test that retrieves remote data with ``@pytest.mark.remote_data``.
Section context: "Tests marked in this way will be skipped by default by ``pytest`` to prevent test runs from taking too long."
Notes: Applies only if the test fetches remote data.

Original text: Tests that may retrieve remote data should be marked with the ``@pytest.mark.remote_data`` decorator, or, if a doctest, flagged with the ``REMOTE_DATA`` flag.
Atomic rule: Flag a doctest that retrieves remote data with ``# doctest: +REMOTE_DATA``.
Section context: "To skip tests that require fetching remote data, use the ``REMOTE_DATA`` flag instead. This way they can be turned on using the ``--remote-data`` flag when running the tests."
Notes: Applies only if a doctest fetches remote data. Different artifact from the pytest marker rule.

Original text: Some tests involve writing files. These files should not be saved permanently. The :ref:`pytest 'tmp_path' fixture <pytest:tmp_path>` allows for the convenient creation of temporary directories, which ensures test files will be cleaned up.
Atomic rule: Write files created by a test into the ``tmp_path`` fixture directory rather than a permanent location.
Section context: "Temporary directories can also be helpful in the case where the tests are run in an environment where ``pytest`` would otherwise not have write access."
Notes: Applies only if the test writes files.

Original text: As a guideline, use ``parametrize`` if you can enumerate all possible test cases and each failure would be a distinct issue, and Hypothesis when there are many possible inputs or you only want a single simple failure to be reported.
Atomic rule: Use ``@pytest.mark.parametrize`` for enumerable cases and Hypothesis when the input space is large.
Section context: Explicitly framed as "a guideline"; both tools are sanctioned and the split is a judgment about the input space.
Notes: none

Original text: For tests that test functions or methods that require optional dependencies (e.g., Scipy), pytest should be instructed to skip the test if the dependencies are not present, as the ``astropy`` tests should succeed even if an optional dependency is not present.
Atomic rule: Skip a test that needs an optional dependency when that dependency is absent.
Section context: The consequence is stated: the astropy test suite must pass without optional dependencies installed. The example shows ``@pytest.mark.skipif``.
Notes: Applies only if the test needs an optional dependency.

Original text:
``astropy`` provides a list of boolean flags that test whether optional dependencies are installed (at import time). For example, to load the corresponding flag for Scipy and mark a test to skip if Scipy is not present, use::

    from astropy.utils.compat.optional_deps import HAS_SCIPY
Atomic rule: Take the skip condition from the ``HAS_*`` flags in ``astropy.utils.compat.optional_deps``.
Section context: "These variables should exist for all of Astropy's optional dependencies; a complete list of supported flags can be found in ``astropy.utils.compat.optional_deps``."
Notes: Applies only if the test skips on an optional dependency.

Original text: Any new optional dependencies should be added to that file
Atomic rule: Add a ``HAS_*`` flag to ``astropy/utils/compat/optional_deps.py`` for any new optional dependency.
Section context: "that file" is ``astropy.utils.compat.optional_deps``, named in the preceding sentence.
Notes: Applies only if the PR introduces a new optional dependency.

Original text: Any new optional dependencies should be added to that file, as well as to the relevant entries in the ``pyproject.toml`` file in the ``[project.optional-dependencies]`` section; typically, under ``all`` for dependencies used in user-facing code [...] and in ``test_all`` for dependencies only used in tests
Atomic rule: Record a new optional dependency in ``[project.optional-dependencies]`` in ``pyproject.toml``, under ``all`` for runtime use or ``test_all`` for test-only use.
Section context: The section names the two target groups exactly, with worked examples (h5py, skyfield).
Notes: Applies only if the PR introduces a new optional dependency.

Original text: In order to test that warnings are triggered as expected in certain situations, |pytest| provides its own context manager :ref:`pytest.warns <pytest:warns>`
Atomic rule: Assert expected warnings with the ``pytest.warns`` context manager.
Section context: "Note that when no warning of the specified type is triggered, this will make the test fail." The note warns off ``recwarn``: "This method has been found to be problematic in at least one case".
Notes: Applies only if the test checks for a warning.

Original text: tests that are designed to trigger certain errors should verify that an exception of the expected type is raised in the expected place. This is efficiently done by running the tested code inside the :ref:`pytest.raises <pytest:assertraises>` context manager.
Atomic rule: Assert expected exceptions with the ``pytest.raises`` context manager.
Section context: "Its optional ``match`` argument allows to check the error message for any patterns using ``regex`` syntax."
Notes: Applies only if the test checks for an exception.

Original text: you can use the `astropy.config.ConfigItem.set_temp` context manager to temporarily set a configuration item to that value, test within that context, and have it automatically return to its original value.
Atomic rule: Change a configuration item inside a test with the ``ConfigItem.set_temp`` context manager.
Section context: "In order to ensure reproducibility of tests, all configuration items are reset to their default values when ``pytest`` starts up." Phrased as "you can use", with no alternative named.
Notes: Applies only if the test depends on a non-default configuration value.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/testguide.html | Marking blocks of code to exclude from coverage
Original text: Blocks of code may be ignored by the coverage testing by adding a comment containing the phrase ``pragma: no cover`` to the start of the block
Atomic rule: Mark a block excluded from coverage with a ``# pragma: no cover`` comment at its start.
Section context: Purely permissive ("may be ignored") but the marker text and its placement are exact.
Notes: Fires only if the contributor chooses to exclude a block from coverage.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/testguide.html | Image tests with pytest-mpl > Writing image tests
Original text: Rather than use the ``@pytest.mark.mpl_image_compare`` decorator directly, you should make use of the ``@figure_test`` convenience decorator which sets the default tolerance and style to be consistent across the astropy core package, and also automatically enables access to remote data
Atomic rule: Decorate figure tests with ``@figure_test`` from ``astropy.tests.figures`` rather than ``@pytest.mark.mpl_image_compare``.
Section context: The consequence is stated: ``@figure_test`` is what makes tolerance and style consistent across the core package.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds an image/figure test.

Original text: The Astropy test suite automatically detects and runs any doctests in the astropy source code or documentation
Atomic rule: Write docstring and narrative examples so they run correctly as doctests.
Section context: "The idea is to write usage examples in docstrings that users can enter verbatim and check their output against the expected output" - a wrong example is a test failure, not just a typo.
Notes: none

Original text: Next to the example add a comment like: ``# doctest: +SKIP``.
Atomic rule: Mark a non-executable doctest example with ``# doctest: +SKIP``.
Section context: "Sometimes it is necessary to write examples that look like doctests but that are not actually executable verbatim." Four sanctioned mechanisms are listed; this is the per-line one.
Notes: Fires only if the contributor writes a non-executable example.

Original text: Astropy's test framework adds support for a special ``__doctest_skip__`` variable that can be placed at the module level of any module to list functions, classes, and methods in that module whose doctests should not be run. [...] The value of ``__doctest_skip__`` should be a list of wildcard patterns
Atomic rule: Skip a module's doctests by listing wildcard patterns in a module-level ``__doctest_skip__``.
Section context: "To skip all doctests in a module:: ``__doctest_skip__ = ['*']``"; module docstrings are skipped with the string '.'.
Notes: Fires only if the contributor skips doctests at module level.

Original text: ``__doctest_requires__`` is a way to list dependencies for specific doctests. It should be a dictionary mapping wildcard patterns (in the same format as ``__doctest_skip__``) to a list of one or more modules that should be *importable* in order for the tests to run.
Atomic rule: Declare a doctest's optional-dependency requirements in a module-level ``__doctest_requires__`` dictionary.
Section context: "if some tests require the scipy module to work they will be skipped unless ``import scipy`` is possible."
Notes: Fires only if a doctest needs an optional dependency.

Original text: In the Sphinx documentation, a doctest section can be skipped by making it part of a ``doctest-skip`` directive
Atomic rule: Skip a doctest block in narrative documentation with the ``.. doctest-skip::`` directive (or ``.. doctest-skip-all``).
Section context: "It is also possible to skip all doctests below a certain line using a ``doctest-skip-all`` comment. Note the lack of ``::`` at the end of the line here" - the two forms have different syntax.
Notes: Fires only if the contributor skips a doctest in an .rst file.

Original text: In the Sphinx documentation, a doctest requirement can be notated with the ``doctest-requires`` directive
Atomic rule: Gate a doctest block in narrative documentation on a dependency with the ``.. doctest-requires::`` directive.
Section context: Parallel to __doctest_requires__ but for .rst files.
Notes: Fires only if a narrative doctest needs an optional dependency.

Original text: The simplest way to generalize the example output is to use the ellipses ``...``.
Atomic rule: Generalize variable doctest output with ellipses.
Section context: "The doctest system compares the actual output to the example output verbatim by default, but this not always feasible." Named as the "simplest way", with IGNORE_OUTPUT and FLOAT_CMP offered as alternatives.
Notes: none

Original text: Another possibility for ignoring output is to use the ``# doctest: +IGNORE_OUTPUT`` flag.
Atomic rule: Ignore a doctest's output entirely with the ``# doctest: +IGNORE_OUTPUT`` flag.
Section context: "This allows a doctest to execute (and check that the code executes without errors), but allows the entire output to be ignored in cases where we don't care what the output is."
Notes: Fires only if the contributor chooses to ignore doctest output.

Original text: the ``pytest-doctestplus`` plugin provides support for a ``FLOAT_CMP`` flag that can be used with doctests.
Atomic rule: Compare floating-point doctest output with the ``# doctest: +FLOAT_CMP`` flag.
Section context: "Because doctests work by comparing strings this can cause such tests to fail." - a stated consequence for omitting it.
Notes: Applies only if the doctest output contains floating-point values.

Original text: It is suggested that you automate the code-style checks using the provided pre-commit hook, as described in the :ref:`pre-commit` section.
Atomic rule: Automate the code-style checks with the provided pre-commit hook.
Section context: Offered as a suggestion alongside the manual ``tox -e codestyle`` invocation.
Notes: Same obligation as the development_details Pre-commit section.

Original text: You should at least run the relevant tests before you make any changes to make sure that your Python environment is set up properly.
Atomic rule: Run the tests relevant to the code you are about to touch before making any changes.
Section context: "It would be hard to overstate the importance of testing in Astropy." The stated purpose is checking the environment, not the change.
Notes: none

Original text: If the bug you are working on involves remote data access, you need to run the tests with an extra flag, i.e., ``pytest astropy/coordinates/tests --remote-data``.
Atomic rule: Run the tests with ``--remote-data`` when the bug involves remote data access.
Section context: Remote-data tests are skipped by default, so without the flag the relevant tests do not run at all.
Notes: Applies only if the change involves remote data access.

Original text: The goal at this point may be a little counter-intuitive: write a test that we know will fail with the current code. This test allows ``astropy`` to check, in an automated way, whether our fix actually works and to prevent regression
Atomic rule: Write a test that fails before the fix and passes after it.
Section context: The worked example commits the failing test before the fix, then the fix.
Notes: Same obligation as the testguide Regression tests section.

Original text: Give the test a reasonably clear name; e.g., ``test_array_len``.
Atomic rule: Give a new test a clear, descriptive name.
Section context: "The easiest way to figure out what you need to import and how to set up the test is to look at other tests." No naming scheme is published beyond the pytest ``test_`` prefix.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/git_edit_workflow_examples.html | Add this test to your local git repo
Original text: Keep `git`_ commits small and focused on one logical piece at a time.
Atomic rule: Keep each commit small and focused on one logical change.
Section context: "The test we just wrote is one logical change, so we will commit it. You could, if you prefer, wait and commit this test along with your fix." - the section itself sanctions bundling.
Notes: Same obligation as development_details 'Each logical set of changes should be treated as one commit'.

Original text: Commit messages should be concise.
Atomic rule: Keep commit messages concise.
Section context: No length limit is given anywhere in the astropy docs.
Notes: Same obligation as development_details 'Make your git commit messages short and descriptive'.

Original text: Including the GitHub issue number allows GitHub to automatically create links to the relevant issue.
Atomic rule: Include the GitHub issue number in the commit message.
Section context: Stated as a benefit rather than a requirement here; development_details states the same thing with an exact form (``Closes #123``).
Notes: Same obligation as the development_details commit-message note.

Original text: Create a file ``docs/changes/coordinates/<PULL REQUEST>.feature.rst``, where ``<PULL REQUEST>`` is the pull request number (1917 for this example).
Atomic rule: Name the changelog fragment for the pull request number and change type in the sub-package directory.
Section context: "Keeping the list of changes up to date is nearly impossible unless each contributor makes the appropriate updates as they propose changes."
Notes: Same obligation as development_details 'Add a changelog entry' and docs/changes/README.rst.

Original text: The content of this file should summarize what you did.
Atomic rule: Summarize the change in the changelog fragment.
Section context: "For writing changelog entries, you do not need to know much about the markup language being used [...] look at other entries and emulate."
Notes: none

Original text: Putting ``len()`` in double-backtick makes that text render in a monospaced font.
Atomic rule: Wrap code names in the changelog fragment in double backticks.
Section context: Stated as a rendering consequence, in a worked example.
Notes: Same obligation as the development_details changelog backtick rule.

Original text: tl;dr: Never work in your main branch, always work in a feature branch.
Atomic rule: Make changes on a feature branch, never on ``main``.
Section context: Set in an .. Important:: directive; the section then explains the three-way ambiguity of the name ``main``.
Notes: none

Original text: it is never allowed to force push to the main astropy repo (typically called ``upstream``), because this would re-write commit history and thus cause problems for all others.
Atomic rule: Never force-push to the upstream astropy repository.
Section context: "Note that this will overwrite the branch on GitHub, i.e. this is one of the few ways you can actually lose commits with git." Force-pushing your own fork is explicitly allowed.
Notes: none

Original text: Do this only for your own feature branches.
Atomic rule: Rewrite commit history only on your own feature branches.
Section context: Set in a .. note:: directive introducing interactive rebasing.
Notes: none

Original text: Please run `git shortlog -es` locally first with your changes to make sure your edit is correct, and you only appear in the list once.
Atomic rule: Run ``git shortlog -es`` locally to verify a ``.mailmap`` edit before proposing it.
Section context: "If you need to edit .mailmap and know how to do it then you can open a pull request for that." - the whole section is gated on the contributor's own identity record.
Notes: Applies only if the contributor edits .mailmap, which depends on their own name appearing more than once in the history.

Original text: We encourage you to setup and use these hooks to ensure that your code always meets our coding style standards.
Atomic rule: Install and use the project's pre-commit hooks.
Section context: "All of the coding style checks described in :ref:`code-style` can be performed automatically when you make a git commit". The section also names ``tox -e codestyle`` and ``pre-commit run`` as manual alternatives.
Notes: none

Original text: The changes made by ``pre-commit`` will not be automatically staged, so you will need to review and re-stage any files that ``pre-commit`` has changed.
Atomic rule: Review and re-stage any file that pre-commit rewrote before committing.
Section context: Set in a .. note:: directive; the consequence of not doing it is a commit that omits the fixes.
Notes: Fires only if the contributor runs pre-commit and it rewrites a file.

Original text:
If you do not want to use ``pre-commit`` as part of your git workflow, you can still run the checks manually (see, :ref:`code-style`) using::

  tox -e codestyle
Atomic rule: Run ``tox -e codestyle`` if you do not use the pre-commit hooks.
Section context: Explicitly the alternative branch of the pre-commit rule; ``pre-commit run`` is offered as a third route.
Notes: Alternative form of the pre-commit style-check obligation.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text: Each logical set of changes should be treated as one commit. For example, if you are fixing a known bug in Astropy and notice a different bug while implementing your fix, implement the fix to that new bug as a different set of changes.
Atomic rule: Put each logical set of changes in its own commit.
Section context: The worked example in git_edit_workflow_examples nevertheless sanctions committing a test and its fix together.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text: Test that your changes do not lead to *regressions*, i.e. that your changes do not break existing code, by running the Astropy tests as described in :ref:`testing-guidelines`.
Atomic rule: Run the astropy test suite and confirm your changes break no existing test.
Section context: CONTRIBUTING.md's merge checklist restates this as "Does ``tox -e test`` run without failures?"
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text: If appropriate, as when you are adding a new feature, you should update the appropriate documentation in the ``docs`` directory
Atomic rule: Update the narrative documentation in ``docs/`` when you add a feature.
Section context: "If appropriate" leaves the trigger to the contributor; CONTRIBUTING.md states the same obligation unhedged as "be sure to include a description in the main documentation".
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds new functionality. Conflicting strengths with the CONTRIBUTING.md Documentation bullet.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text:
you can also check that the documentation builds and looks correct by running, from the ``astropy`` directory::

     cd docs
     make html

   The last line should just state ``build succeeded``, and should not mention any warnings.
Atomic rule: Build the documentation and confirm it reports ``build succeeded`` with no warnings.
Section context: Gated on "If you have sphinx installed"; CONTRIBUTING.md's checklist asks the same question as a merge condition.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text: Add tests of your new code, if appropriate. Some changes (e.g. to documentation) do not need tests.
Atomic rule: Add tests covering new code.
Section context: "Some changes (e.g. to documentation) do not need tests" is the stated exemption. CONTRIBUTING.md's checklist and the quickstart tips both restate it as a merge condition.
Notes: Applies only if the PR changes code rather than documentation alone.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text: if you have no experience writing tests or with the |pytest| testing framework submit your changes without adding tests, but mention in the pull request that you have not written tests.
Atomic rule: Say in the pull request that you have written no tests when you submit without them.
Section context: An explicit escape hatch from the add-tests rule, conditioned on the contributor's own experience.
Notes: Applies only if the contributor is inexperienced with pytest - a fact about the person, not the change.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text: Make your `git`_ commit messages short and descriptive.
Atomic rule: Keep commit messages short and descriptive.
Section context: Set in a .. note:: directive. No character limit is given anywhere in astropy's docs, unlike django's 72 or sympy's 71.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text: If a commit fixes an issue, include, on the second or later line of the commit message, the issue number in the commit message, like this: ``Closes #123``. Doing so will automatically close the issue when the pull request is accepted.
Atomic rule: Put ``Closes #<issue>`` on the second or a later line of the commit message when the commit fixes an issue.
Section context: The consequence is stated: GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR is accepted. The line position is part of the form.
Notes: Applies only if the commit fixes a reported issue.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | The editing workflow > In more detail
Original text: Some modifications require more than one commit; if in doubt, break your changes into a few, smaller, commits rather than one large commit that does many things at once.
Atomic rule: Split a large change into several smaller commits.
Section context: "if in doubt" - offered as a tiebreaker, not a threshold.
Notes: none

Original text: Add a changelog fragment briefly describing the change you made by creating a new file in ``docs/changes/<sub-package>/``.
Atomic rule: Add a changelog fragment under ``docs/changes/<sub-package>/`` describing your change.
Section context: CONTRIBUTING.md exempts "fixes to bugs introduced in the developer version" and "minor documentation or test updates", and lists the entry on the merge checklist as "If applicable".
Notes: Applies only to user-visible changes: new features, API changes, fixed issues.

Original text:
The file should be named like ``<PULL REQUEST>.<TYPE>.rst``, where ``<PULL REQUEST>`` is a pull request number, and ``<TYPE>`` is one of:

* ``feature``: New feature.
* ``api``: API change.
* ``bugfix``: Bug fix.
* ``perf``: Performance improvement [...]
* ``other``: Other changes and additions.
Atomic rule: Name the changelog fragment ``<PR number>.<feature|api|bugfix|perf|other>.rst``.
Section context: The .pre-commit-config.yaml `changelogs-rst` hook fails any file under docs/changes/<pkg>/ not matching `\d+\.(bugfix|feature|api|perf)(\.\d)?\.rst`.
Notes: "If you are opening a new pull request, you may not know its number yet, but you can add it *after* you make the pull request."

Original text: When writing changelog entries, do not attempt to make API reference links by using single-backticks.
Atomic rule: Do not use single backticks for API reference links in changelog fragments.
Section context: "This is because the changelog (in its current format) runs for the history of the project, and API references you make today may not be valid in a future version of Astropy."
Notes: none

Original text: use of double-backticks for monospace rendering of module/class/function/argument names and the like is encouraged.
Atomic rule: Use double backticks for code names in changelog fragments.
Section context: Stated as the sanctioned counterpart to the single-backtick prohibition.
Notes: none

Original text: Enter a title for the set of changes, and some explanation of what you've done.
Atomic rule: Give the pull request a title and an explanation of the change.
Section context: "If there is anything you'd like particular attention for, like a complicated change or some code you are not happy with, add the details here."
Notes: none

Original text: If you don't think your request is ready to be merged, just say so in your pull request message.
Atomic rule: Say in the pull request when the change is not ready to be merged.
Section context: "This is still a good way to start a preliminary code review." The draft-PR mechanism is offered as the alternative.
Notes: none

Original text: if your commits are not ready for CI testing, you should also use ``[ci skip]`` or ``[skip ci]`` directive in your commit message.
Atomic rule: Put ``[ci skip]`` or ``[skip ci]`` in the commit message when the commits are not ready for CI.
Section context: "You may also opt to open a work-in-progress pull request." CONTRIBUTING.md adds that the two spellings are interchangeable.
Notes: Fires only if the contributor opens work-in-progress commits.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | Do Not Create a Merge Commit
Original text: GitHub might offer you the option to catch up or resolve conflicts via its web interface, but do not use this. Using the web interface might create a "merge commit" in your commit history, which is undesirable
Atomic rule: Do not resolve conflicts through GitHub's web interface.
Section context: "a 'merge commit' can introduce maintenance overhead for the release manager as well as undesirable branch structure complexity."
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | Do Not Create a Merge Commit
Original text: Do not use the ``git pull`` command either.
Atomic rule: Do not update your branch with ``git pull``.
Section context: "Pulling changes from ``astropy/main`` includes merging the branches, which combines them in a way that preserves the commit history of both. The purpose of rebasing is rewriting the commit history of your branch, not preserving it." Set in a .. warning:: directive.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | Do Not Create a Merge Commit
Original text: Instead, in your local checkout, do a ``fetch`` and then a ``rebase``, and resolve conflicts as necessary.
Atomic rule: Bring your branch up to date with ``git fetch`` followed by ``git rebase``.
Section context: Stated as the sanctioned replacement for the web interface and for ``git pull``.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | Rebase if necessary > When to rebase
Original text:
Pull requests **must** be rebased (but not necessarily squashed to a single commit) if at least one of the following conditions is met:

* There are conflicts with ``main``.
* There are commits in ``main`` (after the PR branch point) needed for continuous integration tests to run correctly.
* There are merge commits from ``astropy/main`` in the PR commit history
Atomic rule: Rebase the pull request when it conflicts with ``main``, needs newer ``main`` commits for CI, or carries merge commits from ``astropy/main``.
Section context: "merge commits from PRs to the user's fork are fine" is the stated exception.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | Rebase if necessary > How to rebase
Original text:
before you start make a branch to serve as a backup copy of your work::

    git branch tmp my-new-feature
Atomic rule: Make a backup branch before rebasing.
Section context: "It is easier to make mistakes rebasing than other areas of git".
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | Squash if necessary > When to squash
Original text: If a pull request contains commits with large (approximately > 10KB) intermediate changes which are ultimately removed or modified in the PR, the intermediate diffs **must** be squashed.
Atomic rule: Squash intermediate commits larger than about 10KB whose changes are later removed or modified.
Section context: "The goal is to avoid an unnecessary increase in the size of the ``astropy`` repository." An example is given: adding then removing a large data file.
Notes: none

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/development_details.html | Squash if necessary > When to squash
Original text: Squashing commits is **encouraged** when there are numerous commits which do not add value to the commit history.
Atomic rule: Squash commits that add no value to the history.
Section context: "In general, commits that reflect a specific atomic change (e.g., 'Fixed bug revealed by tests for feature X') may have value for the history." A list of good squash candidates follows.
Notes: none

Original text:
Use of a simple ``git push`` will be prevented because of the changed history, and will need to be manually overridden using::

    git push origin my-new-feature --force
Atomic rule: Force-push to your own fork after rebasing.
Section context: Paired with the git_resources prohibition on force-pushing to upstream.
Notes: Fires only if the contributor rebased an already-pushed branch.

Original text: All code must be compatible with the versions of Python indicated by the ``requires-python`` key  under ``[project]`` in the `pyproject.toml <https://github.com/astropy/astropy/blob/main/pyproject.toml>`_ file of the core package.
Atomic rule: Keep all code compatible with the Python versions in ``requires-python`` in ``pyproject.toml``.
Section context: The supported range is not written in the prose; it is read out of pyproject.toml, which the docs link to.
Notes: CONTRIBUTING.md's merge checklist asks the same question.

Original text: The core package should be importable with no dependencies other than components already in the Astropy core, the `Python Standard Library <https://docs.python.org/3/library/index.html>`_, and |NumPy| |minimum_numpy_version| or later.
Atomic rule: Keep the core package importable using only the standard library, NumPy, and astropy itself.
Section context: The next bullet carves out the exception: additional dependencies are allowed inside sub-modules and function calls, not at import time.
Notes: none

Original text: Additional dependencies - such as |SciPy|, |Matplotlib|, or other third-party packages - are allowed for sub-modules or in function calls, but they must be noted in the package documentation
Atomic rule: Document any additional third-party dependency a sub-module or function introduces.
Section context: The permission and the obligation are in one sentence: allowed, but only if documented.
Notes: Applies only if the PR introduces a third-party dependency.

Original text: Additional dependencies [...] should only affect the relevant component.
Atomic rule: Confine an additional dependency's effect to the component that needs it.
Section context: Read together with the import-time rule above; states a property of the result rather than a form.
Notes: Applies only if the PR introduces a third-party dependency.

Original text: In functions and methods, the optional dependency should use a normal ``import`` statement, which will raise an ``ImportError`` if the dependency is not available.
Atomic rule: Import an optional dependency with a plain ``import`` inside the function or method that uses it.
Section context: The consequence is stated in the same sentence: a plain import is what produces the ImportError users are meant to see. CONTRIBUTING.md's checklist asks "Do functions that require additional dependencies raise an ``ImportError`` if they are not present?"
Notes: Applies only if the code uses an optional dependency.

Original text: In the astropy core package, such optional dependencies should be recorded in the ``pyproject.toml`` file in the ``[project.optional-dependencies]`` entry (put it in the appropriate category of optional dependencies).
Atomic rule: Record an optional dependency in ``[project.optional-dependencies]`` in ``pyproject.toml``.
Section context: The parenthesis names the sub-decision; testguide names the categories (``all``, ``test_all``) exactly.
Notes: Applies only if the PR introduces an optional dependency. Same file and section as the testguide optional-dependency rule.

Original text:
At the module level, one can subclass a class from an optional dependency like so::

      try:
          from opdep import Superclass
      except ImportError:
          warn(AstropyWarning('opdep is not present, so <functionality>'
                              'will not work.'))
          class Superclass: pass
Atomic rule: Guard a module-level import from an optional dependency with try/except ImportError and a fallback that warns.
Section context: "one can" - offered as a worked pattern for the module-level case the plain-import rule cannot cover.
Notes: Applies only if a module-level class inherits from an optional dependency.

Original text: General utilities necessary for but not specific to the package or sub-package should be placed in a ``packagename.utils`` module (e.g. ``astropy.utils`` for the core package).
Atomic rule: Put general-purpose utilities in ``astropy.utils`` rather than in a sub-package.
Section context: none
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a utility that is not specific to one sub-package.

Original text: If a utility is already present in :mod:`astropy.utils`, packages should always use that utility instead of re-implementing it in ``packagename.utils`` module.
Atomic rule: Use an existing ``astropy.utils`` utility instead of re-implementing it.
Section context: "always" removes the discretion the surrounding bullets otherwise allow.
Notes: none

Original text: Docstrings must be present for all public classes/methods/functions
Atomic rule: Give every public class, method, and function a docstring.
Section context: docguide restates it as "Docstrings must be provided for all public classes, methods, and functions"; CONTRIBUTING.md's checklist asks the same.
Notes: none

Original text: [Docstrings] must follow the form outlined in the :doc:`docguide` document.
Atomic rule: Write docstrings in the form the documentation guidelines set out.
Section context: A pointer; docguide names the actual form (numpydoc).

Original text: Write usage examples in the docstrings of all classes and functions whenever possible.
Atomic rule: Include a usage example in the docstring of a class or function.
Section context: "whenever possible" sanctions omission; CONTRIBUTING.md's checklist asks for "An example of running the code?".
Notes: none

Original text: These examples should be short and simple to reproduce--users should be able to copy them verbatim and run them.
Atomic rule: Keep docstring examples short and runnable verbatim.
Section context: No length or complexity bound is offered.
Notes: none

Original text: These examples should, whenever possible, be in the :ref:`doctest <doctests>` format and will be executed as part of the test suite.
Atomic rule: Write docstring examples in doctest format.
Section context: "whenever possible"; the consequence is that they run as tests, which testguide's Writing doctests section covers.
Notes: none

Original text: Unit tests should be provided for as many public methods and functions as possible, and should adhere to the standards set in the :doc:`testguide` document.

Atomic rule: Keep in-repository data files under about 100 kB and host anything larger off the repository.

Original text: These data should always be accessed via the :func:`~astropy.utils.data.get_pkg_data_fileobj` or :func:`~astropy.utils.data.get_pkg_data_filename` functions.
Atomic rule: Access package data through ``get_pkg_data_fileobj`` or ``get_pkg_data_filename``.

Notes: none

Original text:
``astropy`` source code should contain a comment at the beginning of the file pointing to the license for the ``astropy`` source code.  This line should say::

Original text: When a list or array should be formatted as one item per line then this is best achieved by using the `magic trailing comma`
Atomic rule: Use a magic trailing comma to keep a list or array formatted one item per line.
Section context: Set in a .. note:: under the formatting-suppression paragraph, offered as the preferred alternative to disabling ruff formatting.
Notes: Fires only if the contributor wants a literal kept one item per line.

Original text: Classes should either use direct variable access, or Python's property mechanism for setting object instance variables. ``get_value``/``set_value`` style methods should be used only when getting and setting the values requires a computationally-expensive operation.
Atomic rule: Expose instance state through attributes or properties rather than get_/set_ methods unless access is computationally expensive.
Section context: The Examples section shows the intended and unintended forms side by side, labelling ``s.set_color(0.4)`` "Bad form!".
Notes: none

Original text: Classes should use the builtin `super` function when making calls to methods in their super-class(es) unless there are specific reasons not to.
Atomic rule: Call super-class methods through ``super()``.
Section context: "`super` should be used consistently in all subclasses since it does not work otherwise." The super() vs direct-calling example shows the broken MRO that results.
Notes: none

Original text: Multiple inheritance should be avoided in general without good reason. [...] Non-trivial multiple-inheritance schemes should not be attempted without good justification
Atomic rule: Avoid non-trivial multiple inheritance.
Section context: "However, trivial multiple inheritance using orthogonal base classes, known as the 'mixin' pattern, may be used."
Notes: none

Original text: ``__init__.py`` files for modules should not contain any significant implementation code.
Atomic rule: Keep implementation code out of ``__init__.py``.
Section context: "``__init__.py`` can contain docstrings and code for organizing the module layout, however (e.g. ``from submodule import *`` in accord with the guideline above)."
Notes: none

Original text: If a module is small enough that it fits in one file, it should simply be a single file, rather than a directory with an ``__init__.py`` file.
Atomic rule: Keep a small module as a single file rather than a package directory.
Section context: "small enough that it fits in one file" is the only threshold offered.
Notes: none

Original text: Command-line scripts should follow the form outlined in the :doc:`scripts` document.
Atomic rule: Follow the command-line script conventions in the scripts document.
Section context: A pointer; the scripts page states the actual form.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a command-line script. Same obligation as the scripts page rules.

Original text: `~object.__repr__`: Return a `str` containing only ASCII characters. The output must be independent of the ``astropy.conf.unicode_output`` setting.
Atomic rule: Make ``__repr__`` return ASCII-only text regardless of ``unicode_output``.
Section context: "For maximum compatibility, we need to assume that writing non-ASCII characters to the console or to files will not work." A test helper, ``assert_follows_unicode_guidelines``, exists to check this.
Notes: Applies only if the class implements string conversion methods.

Original text: `~object.__str__`: Return a `str` containing only ASCII characters if ``astropy.conf.unicode_output`` is `False`.
Atomic rule: Make ``__str__`` and ``__format__`` return ASCII-only text when ``unicode_output`` is False.
Section context: ``__format__`` carries the same rule with the extra condition that ``format_spec`` is empty. Both may return non-ASCII when the setting is True.
Notes: Applies only if the class implements string conversion methods.

Original text: For classes that are expected to roundtrip through strings, the parser must accept the output of `~object.__str__`.
Atomic rule: Make a round-trippable class's parser accept its own ``__str__`` output.
Section context: "This design generally follows `Postel's Law`: 'Be liberal in what you accept, and conservative in what you send.'"
Notes: Applies only if the class is expected to round-trip through strings.

Original text: C extensions are only allowed when they provide a significant performance enhancement over pure Python, or a robust C library already exists to provided the needed functionality.
Atomic rule: Add a C extension only for a significant performance gain or to wrap an existing C library.
Section context: "significant" is the only threshold; no benchmark is required.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a C extension.

Original text: When C extensions are used, the Python interface must meet the aforementioned Python interface guidelines.
Atomic rule: Make a C extension's Python interface meet the same interface guidelines as pure Python code.
Section context: "aforementioned" points back at the Interface and Dependencies section on the same page.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a C extension. Restates the Interface and Dependencies rules for C code.

Original text: The use of Cython_ is strongly recommended for C extensions.
Atomic rule: Write C extensions in Cython.
Section context: "In cases where C extensions are needed but Cython_ cannot be used, the `PEP 7 Style Guide for C Code` is recommended."
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a C extension.

Original text: Cython_ extensions should store ``.pyx`` files in the source code repository
Atomic rule: Commit the ``.pyx`` sources of a Cython extension.
Section context: Paired in one sentence with the prohibition on committing generated .c files.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a Cython extension.

Original text: Cython_ extensions should store ``.pyx`` files in the source code repository, but not the generated ``.c`` files.
Atomic rule: Do not commit the ``.c`` files Cython generates.
Section context: The ccython page reinforces it: the ``.pyx`` files, not the generated ``.c`` files, must be given as the extension source.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a Cython extension.

Original text: If a C extension has a dependency on an external C library, the source code for the library should be bundled with the Astropy core, provided the license for the C library is compatible with the Astropy license.
Atomic rule: Bundle the source of an external C library a C extension depends on, if its license permits.
Section context: The license compatibility condition is written into the rule. cextern/ holds the bundled copies and is excluded from pre-commit.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a C extension with an external C library dependency.

Original text: the package must be compatible with using a system-installed library in place of the library included in Astropy, and a user installing the package should be able to opt-in to using the system version using a ``ASTROPY_USE_SYSTEM_???`` environment variable, where ``???`` is the name of the library, e.g. ``ASTROPY_USE_SYSTEM_WCSLIB``
Atomic rule: Let a bundled C library be replaced by the system copy through an ``ASTROPY_USE_SYSTEM_<LIB>`` environment variable.
Section context: development_details lists the existing variables and the ``ASTROPY_USE_SYSTEM_ALL`` catch-all.
Notes: Applies only if the PR bundles an external C library.

Original text: In cases where C extensions are needed but Cython_ cannot be used, the `PEP 7 Style Guide for C Code <https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0007/>`_ is recommended.
Atomic rule: Follow PEP 7 in hand-written C extension code.
Section context: Explicitly the fallback branch of the Cython recommendation.
Notes: External standard; one pointer rule. Applies only if the PR adds non-Cython C code.

Atomic rule: Declare a C extension's build information through the documented extension mechanism.

Original text: This is optional, but *highly recommended*. `Pre-commit <https://pre-commit.com/>`_ is a tool that runs a number of :ref:`Continuous Integration (CI) <contributing.ci>` checks (e.g. code formatting) on your code before you commit it.

Source: https://docs.astropy.org/en/latest/development/quickstart.html | Creating and submitting a pull request
Original text: If you are new to the Astropy Project and interested to submit a large patch (e.g., a new big feature or significant refactoring), we encourage you to first discuss your ideas on GitHub to increase the chance of your PR being accepted.

Section context: Set in a .. note:: directive. codeguide states the repository half of the same rule: commit .pyx, not the generated .c.
Notes: Applies only if the PR declares a Cython extension through get_extensions.

Original text: When doing this, you should use ``numpy.get_include()`` to specify the include directory to use
Atomic rule: Locate the numpy C headers with ``numpy.get_include()``.
Section context: "If your C or Cython extensions uses `numpy` at the C level, you probably need access to the numpy C headers." A worked example follows.
Notes: Applies only if the extension uses numpy at the C level.

Original text: 1) Create an ``include`` directory inside of your package for all of the header files.
Atomic rule: Put a package's installable C header files in an ``include`` directory inside the package.
Section context: "If your C extension needs to be linked from other third-party C code, you probably want to install its header files along side the Python module."
Notes: Applies only if the PR ships C header files for third-party linking.

Original text: 2) Use the ``[tool.setuptools.package_data]`` section in your ``pyproject.toml`` file to include those header files in the package.
Atomic rule: Declare installable C header files in ``[tool.setuptools.package_data]`` in ``pyproject.toml``.
Section context: The worked example is `astropy.wcs`: ``"astropy.wcs" = ["include/*/*.h"]``.
Notes: Applies only if the PR ships C header files for third-party linking.

Original text: It is important to make sure that ``setup_package.py`` files do not trigger an import of the package they are in - so they should be able to be executed without relying on imports to other parts of the package.
Atomic rule: Keep ``setup_package.py`` free of imports from the package it belongs to.
Section context: The whole section exists for this one obligation; the consequence is a build-time import failure.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds or edits a setup_package.py.

Original text: Command-line scripts in Astropy should follow a consistent scheme to promote readability and compatibility.
Atomic rule: Follow the standard scheme for command-line scripts.

Original text: They should have a ``main`` function to parse the arguments and pass those arguments on to some library function so that the library function can be used programmatically when needed.
Atomic rule: Give a command-line script a ``main`` function that parses arguments and delegates to a library function.

Original text: The ``main`` function should accept an optional single argument that holds the ``sys.argv`` list, except for the script name (e.g., ``argv[1:]``).
Atomic rule: Give ``main`` a single optional argument holding ``sys.argv[1:]``.
Section context: The example signature is ``def main(args=None):``.
Notes: Applies only if the PR adds a command-line script.

Original text: It must then be added to the list of entry points in the ``setup.py`` file (see the example below).

Original text:
Each file should be named like ``<PULL REQUEST>.<TYPE>.rst``, where ``<PULL REQUEST>`` is a pull request number, and ``<TYPE>`` is one of:

* ``feature``: New feature.
* ``api``: API change.
* ``bugfix``: Bug fix.
* ``perf``: Performance improvement (this should be significant enough to be measurable using the public API).
* ``other``: Other changes and additions.
Atomic rule: Name each changelog fragment ``<PR number>.<type>.rst`` using one of the five published types.
Section context: The .pre-commit-config.yaml `changelogs-rst` hook fails on any other name under docs/changes/<pkg>/.
Notes: Same obligation as the development_details fragment-naming rule.

Original text: If the change concerns a sub-package, the file should go in the sub-directory relative to this sub-package.
Atomic rule: Put a sub-package's changelog fragment in that sub-package's directory under ``docs/changes/``.
Section context: The pre-commit hook keys on the path ``^docs/changes/[\w\.]+/``.
Notes: Same obligation as the development_details fragment-location rule.

Original text: Type ``other`` is not allowed in sub-directories.
Atomic rule: Put ``other``-type changelog fragments only in the root ``docs/changes/`` directory.
Section context: A second pre-commit hook, `changelogs-rst-other`, fails any non-``other`` file placed in the root directory, so the constraint runs both ways.
Notes: Applies only if the fragment is of type ``other``.

Original text: Note the use of double-backticks for code.
Atomic rule: Use double backticks around code in a changelog fragment.
Section context: Follows the worked ``123.feature.rst`` example, which uses them throughout.
Notes: Same obligation as the development_details changelog backtick rule.
